LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_le_log_ca: On a nonempty finite alphabet A, every law p satisfies H(p) ≤ ln |A| nats.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_le_log_su: For a law p on a finite alphabet, H(p) ≤ ln |supp(p)|, the logarithm of the number of outcomes of positive probability.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyOf_le_log_: For a finite-valued variable X, H(X) is at most the logarithm of the number of values X attains with positive probability.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_uniformOf: The uniform law on a nonempty finite set A has entropy ln |A| nats.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_eq_log_ca: A probability law p on a nonempty finite set A has H(p) = ln |A| if and only if it is uniform on all of A.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_eq_log_su: A finite law p has entropy ln |supp(p)| exactly when p assigns equal mass to all outcomes in its support.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyOf_eq_log_: For a finite-valued variable X with nonempty alphabet A, H(X) equals ln |A| exactly when X has the uniform distribution on A.
The entropy of a finite-valued X equals the logarithm of the size of its support exactly when all its positive-probability values are equally likely.
